findings.claim: The change modifies MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000. This is unrelated to REQ-2283 and weakens a security default. The ledger records a stack depth limit of 500 even for trusted data as a deliberate hardening, and 5000 raises the stack-overflow/DoS risk on untrusted input.

receipt_plan.detail: [L9] records the secure-by-default history and a stack depth limit of 500. Also run a test that deserializes a 1000-deep nested payload with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData and expects MessagePackSerializationException, which now fails to throw.

findings.claim: Metadata-only types are deliberately not analysed and get no diagnostics from the compiling assembly. Dropping diagnostics with no location in the compilation (ReportIfLocatedInCompilation) and the new docs saying the defining assembly reports its own problems are consistent with this convention.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed; the defining assembly owns validation of its own types.

findings.claim: The docs state that a defining assembly reports diagnostics for its own members. For a closed generic from a NuGet package built before this analyzer existed, or built without the analyzer, no one ever reports. The README and MsgPack004.md claims are broader than what is guaranteed. The ledger covers this behavior, so this is low risk.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types.
